title: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
capsule: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia was founded on 23 September 1932 when Ibn Saud (Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd al-Rahman Al Saud) united the Hejaz and Nejd under a single crown, completing two decades of military campaigning that had begun with his capture of Riyadh in 1902. The discovery of oil in commercial quantities at Dammam in 1938 transformed the kingdom into one of the world's leading petroleum exporters, and Saudi Arabia became a founding member of OPEC in 1960. The kingdom has remained an absolute monarchy under the Al Saud family, with King Salman (since 2015) and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman directing a state-led modernization program while wielding decisive regional influence through Sunni religious authority and oil wealth.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Borders are defined by a series of treaties (1913–2000) and are well-documented for international boundaries, though the southern frontier with Yemen was disputed into the 2000 Treaty of Jeddah; internal administrative divisions are based on Saudi government records.
